newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-HIGH-SCORING STUTTGART HIT ANOTHER FOUR PAST DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HIGH-SCORING STUTTGART HIT ANOTHER FOUR PAST DORTMUND.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart intensified the race for the German league championship when they ended a remarkable week by blasting four goals past leaders Borussia Dortmund on Saturday.

A 44th-minute penalty from Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov and goals from Dutchman Frank Verlaat, Brazilian striker Giovane Elber and Croat Zvonimir Soldo helped Stuttgart to a 4-1 win which set up a tight situation at the top of the Bundesliga.

Just two points now separate the leading four -- Dortmund, Bayern Munich, Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen. After scoring an astonishing total of 13 goals in three games in the last eight days, Stuttgart are firmly back in the race.

Reigning champions Dortmund, who went ahead in Stuttgart with an eighth-minute goal from Germany defender Stefan Reuter, stayed on top of the table but Bayern drew level on points after a 3-0 victory over Schalke in Munich's Olympic stadium.
Stuttgart are now just two points behind in third place, ahead of Bayer Leverkusen on goal difference. Leverkusen won 1-0 at home against promoted Arminia Bielefeld.

Stuttgart played the most entertaining football in the Bundesliga in the first half of the season. They seem to have hit form again in the last week with high-scoring wins over Hamburg, Cologne and Dortmund.
VfB put on a brilliant show in front of a full house of 53,000 in the Gottlieb-Daimler stadium.
After Reuter put the visitors ahead, Stuttgart refused to panic and took the game by storm in an exciting period at the end of the first half.

The home side equalised in the 44th minute when Dortmund's German international defender Juergen Kohler was judged to have brought down Elber in the area. Balakov struck the ball from the spot perfectly into the left-hand corner.

The reigning champions were clearly angered by the decision and seemed to lose control. Seconds before halftime Verlaat fired in a spectacular left-foot shot from some 20 metres out to put Stuttgart 2-1 in front.

Elber looked more and more dangerous as the game went on. In the 82nd minute he beat Dortmund's offside trap with a well-timed run from his own half, raced away from the defence and struck the ball with composure inside the left-hand post.
Dortmund were destroyed psychologically and two minutes later Soldo finished off the match with another spectacular long-range shot into the roof of the net.

"We put them under pressure in the second half but it was not enough. It was never a penalty," said Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld, who must now lift his team before their European Cup quarter-final second leg at France's Auxerre on Wednesday.

After two defeats in the last week Bayern were happy just to have picked up some points at home against Schalke after goals from Thomas Helmer, Christian Nerlinger and Juergen Klinsmann in the 13th, 89th and 90th minutes.
Schalke have just a few days to bounce back before they travel to Spain to meet Valencia in the UEFA Cup quarter-finals on Tuesday.

Leverkusen, who just managed to avoid relegation last season, needed a goal four minutes from the end from Dutch striker Erik Meijer to secure their victory over Bielefeld, who finished with nine men after two late dismissals.
